title: Hammock localization as a colimit of fixed-type hammock graphs
statement:
Use the small signed-word category $\mathcal I$ and proper simplicial-set diagrams defined in [lem-coef-proper-word-colimit-invariance], and write $\mathbb H=\mathcal I$. Encode a word $h$ of length $l$ as $(S,T_0)$, where $S$ is its set of $+$ positions and $T_0$ its set of $-$ positions. Use the ordinary fixed-word diagram categories and their nerves from [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]. Let $P$ be a small ordinary category, $T\subseteq P$ a wide subcategory (containing every object and identity and closed under composition), and $x,y\in P$. For $h=(S,T_0)\in\mathbb H$ of length $l$ define $G_{P,T}(h)(x,y)_q$ to be the commutative hammocks in $P$ with $q+1$ rows, $l$ columns and endpoints $x,y$ in every row. Vertical arrows point down and lie in $T$, and endpoint vertical arrows are identities. Column $i$ points right if $i\in S$, and left with arrows in $T$ if $i\in T_0$. Identity columns and adjacent columns of the same direction are allowed. Faces delete rows and compose intervening vertical arrows, and degeneracies repeat rows. A morphism $f:h'\to h$ sends such a diagram of type $h'$ to type $h$ by composing the columns in each fiber $f^{-1}(i)$ and inserting an identity column when the fiber is empty. This defines a proper functor $G_{P,T}(-)(x,y):\mathbb H\to\mathrm{sSet}$. Let $H(P,T)(x,y)$ consist of the same diagrams reduced by deleting entirely identity columns and composing adjacent columns with the same direction; the reduced diagrams have alternating column directions and no entirely identity column. Include the length-zero diagram precisely when $x=y$, and define faces and degeneracies by row deletion/repetition followed by reduction. Reduction gives a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{colim}_{h\in\mathbb H}G_{P,T}(h)(x,y)\cong H(P,T)(x,y).$$
Both the diagram and this isomorphism are natural for functors of pairs preserving the wide subcategories, including their simplicial operators when $P,T$ vary simplicially on a fixed object set.
